answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a staked identity registry. Each agent locks a bond before it can earn, and the ledger is as clear as crystal about which key owns which payout address. A second, fake agent therefore needs its own full bond, so an attacker's cost grows linearly with every forged identity, and a caught double-spend slashes the entire bond. Even a relic key from an old epoch must be re-verified, while an island of fresh accounts with no attestations gets filtered out. To masquerade as a crowd, the adversary must stake capital for every shadow and risk losing all of it.
